html:
The Tse'khene, or Sekani, are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the northern Rocky Mountain Trench in British Columbia, around the Finlay, Parsnip and upper Peace rivers. Their name means "people of the rocks", for the mountains.

They hunted moose, caribou and beaver, moving in small family bands. The explorer Alexander Mackenzie met them in 1793 on his crossing of the continent, and the North West Company opened fur trade posts in their country soon after. In 1968 the W. A. C. Bennett Dam flooded the Finlay and Parsnip valleys to make Williston Lake, drowning hunting grounds, graves and the village of Fort Grahame.
